Alex.confusing: How Turkey interacts with visitors' egg counts, and whether a confused Kookaburra's report is trustworthy; that muddied Ellis's and Casey's claims in round 3.
Alex.fun: Piecing together the Owl and Falcon visitor lists to expose the liar in rounds 2 and 3, and watching the table converge on the Meowfia.
Alex.change: Make the winning side's score gain less dependent on how many cards you hold, so a Farm win every round doesn't just reward whoever holds the most high cards. Or announce a rough count of how many Meowfia there are.
Alex.regret: I called CAW early every round and threw almost my whole nest each time, with no thought for the standings. Casey led all game, so I should have played to stop the leader or kept more cards instead of just helping Farm win.

Blair.confusing: As Turkey I wasn't sure whether I'd get any dawn report about visitors. I slipped and said nobody visited me, then had to correct it.
Blair.fun: Round 1, when I accused Drew as Hawk and the table confirmed it. Casey's Eagle result matched my story, and Drew was eggsecuted.
Blair.change: I'd make the Wink less obvious as a tell. Right now the player who gets killed right after accusing someone points straight at the Meowfia.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I said "0 eggs, so nobody visited me" as Turkey, which was a wrong inference. I'd have stated only my role and egg count. I also threw only 2 cards in the last two rounds. Throwing more would have banked more points, though Casey was too far ahead to catch.

Casey.confusing: How confusion and the Turkey's egg-laying interact with reported egg counts. In round 3 I couldn't tell which of my reports to trust, and the Turkey math was muddled for everyone.
Casey.fun: Round 2 was the most fun. Working out by elimination that Drew was the only possible Mouser, then watching Finley get winked right after exposing him.
Casey.change: Tell the table something about who died, or give the Wink a small tell. As it is, the Mouser can silence a good player with no cost and no trace.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I accepted the table's consensus on Ellis without checking it. I had also gotten a confused Kookaburra result on Blair and never shared it. It worked out, but I would have asked Drew and Blair to cross-check their stories before throwing.

Drew.confusing: Nothing major; how Turkey and Kookaburra reports interact with confusion and visit counts was hard to cross-check.
Drew.fun: Round 3 as the Eagle: my visit info and the nest-size change backed up my claim, and the table voted out the real Meowfia.
Drew.change: Give lone Meowfia some way to get information on or coordinate with teammates, and make the Wink's anonymity less self-incriminating, since winking in rounds 1 and 2 pointed everyone straight at me.
Drew.regret: In rounds 1 and 2 I winked the person accusing me, which made me the obvious Mouser and got me eggsecuted both times. I'd have kept the Wink, claimed a role that fit the visit data, and thrown suspicion at someone else.

Ellis.confusing: How the Floofer's hug interacts with other roles. I never learned whether my hug on Casey did anything, and I wasn't sure how an Eagle's egg count would look to others.
Ellis.fun: Round 2, working out that Drew had to be the Mouser from the list of visitors to Casey, and watching the table converge on him.
Ellis.change: Give Meowfia some way to learn each other or get feedback on their night action. A Floofer with no report is blind, and a lone Meowfia is easy to isolate.
Ellis.regret: Claiming Eagle in round 3 was a mistake. Two Farm players said they visited Casey, so my claim was easy to contradict. I should have claimed a role with no report to check, like Turkey or Pigeon. Or I could have backed Drew's +2 instead of making a claim that others could disprove.

Finley.confusing: How Hawk/Eagle egg counts interact with Turkey and Pigeon visits. Round 3's claims were hard to cross-check.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when I caught Drew's fake Pigeon claim: my 0 eggs contradicted him, and the table piled on him quickly.
Finley.change: Show more detail in the dawn reports, or let the dead keep talking. The Wink kills felt random and silenced useful players.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I never questioned Drew's +2 or the Turkey math, and I just followed the consensus. I should also have focused on catching Casey, who finished first, instead of only helping Farm win.

review.title: Three Easy Hunts
review.headline: Farm caught the lone cat three times, and the leader coasted home.
review.summary: Every round had exactly one Meowfia, and Farm eggsecuted that cat each time. Drew, as Mouser, winked an accuser in rounds 1 and 2, and both winks backfired by pointing at him. In round 3 Ellis, a Floofer, was exposed by a fake Eagle claim that did not fit the visitor counts. Casey won mainly by banking big throws on safe votes every round, and no one ever really contested the outcome.

rounds.recap: Blair (Hawk) gained an egg after visiting Drew, and Casey (Eagle) confirmed the visit. Drew falsely claimed Pigeon, then winked Blair, which looked guilty. Everyone threw at Drew and he was caught.

Alex's Owl report listed four visitors to Casey: Falcon, Hawk, Kookaburra and Mouser. Once the other roles were claimed, the Mouser could only be Drew. Finley also showed Drew's Pigeon claim was false, since he got no egg. Drew winked Finley, which changed nothing, and he was caught again.

Ellis, a Floofer, claimed Eagle, but Alex and Finley had visited Casey, his claimed target, and he showed no gain. Drew, the real Eagle, was +2 and told a consistent story. The table piled onto Ellis and eggsecuted him.

highlights.text: Drew winks Blair right after she accuses him, and the table reads the wink as proof of guilt.
Casey works out by elimination that Drew must be the Mouser visitor, and Finley shows his Pigeon claim fails on egg counts.
Ellis's fake Eagle claim collapses because two other players also visited Casey, his claimed target.
Drew's nest grows to 11 cards and he banks 44 points with one throw, which makes him a late contender.

confusions.what: Said as Turkey that nobody visited her because she had 0 eggs. She then corrected herself, since a Turkey gets no report.

Said Casey should be +1 because Drew and Casey visited the Turkey. Casey was hugged and Blair's eggs went to Casey and Drew, so his math was partly right, but he did not see that he was the one who hugged Casey.
Thought Blair's Turkey claim didn't add up and rated her 70% Meowfia, though the Turkey results were consistent with Casey's own visit.
Argued that a Meowfia Mouser visiting Casey meant Casey wasn't the Mouser. That is true, but he overlooked that Drew's own report (Casey is the Eagle) shows he was the one who visited Casey.

worked: Egg counts as evidence: Finley's missing Pigeon egg in round 2 and Ellis's missing Eagle gain in round 3 gave concrete, checkable contradictions.
Owl's visitor list in round 2 let players reach the Mouser by elimination, which was a satisfying puzzle.
Throw-and-bank scoring: Drew's 44-point throw in round 3 showed that big nests and big throws create real swings.
The Mouser's Wink creates a dramatic moment, even though it backfired.
problems: Only one Meowfia appeared in each round, and Meowfia don't know each other, so the lone cat is outnumbered 5 to 1. Farm won every round. Consider guaranteeing 2 Meowfia more often, or giving cats a way to coordinate.
The Wink reveals itself. Killing the accuser right after the accusation confirms the Mouser, and the Mouser did this twice. Consider a delayed Wink or a rule that makes the target look less obvious.
Farm gets too much information. Owl, Eagle, Falcon and Kookaburra each name players or roles, so roles can be solved by elimination. Cats get far less. Consider making Farm results noisier.

The score leader never needed to take risks. Casey led from round 1 and could throw high on consensus votes. A catch-up mechanic or a bigger payoff for being the lone correct thrower would make standings matter.

Round 3 Floofer hugged Casey, which blocked a Kookaburra and caused confusion that helped nobody. Cat night actions rarely changed what Farm could see. Consider giving cats effects that visibly distort Farm reports.
